<action type="say">
Your “Composting Workshop” event is on the calendar.

Event details
- Title: Composting Workshop  
- Date: Sunday, December 14, 2025  
- Time: 1:00–3:00 pm Central Time  
- Location: Community Garden, Madison, WI  
- Attendee (calendar invite): marcus.lee@midwesttrialconsulting.com  
- Event ID (for reference): evt_9f3c72b1c4c8472ab8f6f0f6a3d4c915  
Note: Your calendar system auto-generated an online meeting link; you can ignore/remove it since this is in-person only.

Logistics & materials checklist (concise)
Site & setup
- Confirm specific spot in the garden with:
  - Shade (tree, canopy, or pop-up tent)
  - Access to water (hose or spigot)
  - Space for ~10–20 people to gather around a demo area
- Seating: a few chairs/benches for elders/folks who need to sit
- Weather backup: 
  - Pop-up canopy OR
  - Agreement to move to a nearby sheltered spot if light rain

Materials for demonstration
- Compost examples:
  - One active compost pile (or bin) you can turn
  - One finished compost sample (in a bucket/tub) to show texture/smell
- “Ingredients” props:
  - Browns: dry leaves, shredded paper/cardboard
  - Greens: veggie scraps, coffee grounds, plant trimmings (no meat/dairy)
- Tools:
  - Pitchfork or compost aerator
  - Shovel
  - Buckets/tubs for showing layering or mixing
  - Wheelbarrow (optional, but useful)
- Water:
  - Hose with nozzle or watering can to demo “damp sponge” moisture level
- Protective / cleanliness items:
  - Work gloves (a few extra pairs in assorted sizes)
  - Hand sanitizer or handwashing setup
  - Trash/compost collection buckets for any demo scraps

Signage & info
- Simple signs:
  - “Composting Workshop – Today 1–3 pm”
  - Arrows from garden entrance to the workshop area
- Quick visuals:
  - One-page or flipchart sheet with:
    - “Greens vs Browns”
    - “What’s OK / What to Avoid”
    - Basic recipe: “3 parts browns : 1 part greens”
- Handouts (optional but helpful):
  - Basic how-to compost at home
  - Contact info or website for follow-up questions

Participant comfort
- Encourage attendees (in your promo) to:
  - Wear closed-toe shoes
  - Dress in layers for ~57°F and partly cloudy
- Bring:
  - Reusable water bottles
- You bring:
  - Water cooler or jug (if no fountain nearby)
  - Name tags and markers (optional, but good for community-building)

Simple 2-hour run-of-show
0:00–0:10 – Welcome & intros
- Greet people as they arrive, quick sign-in if you want.
- Brief intro: who you are, what the workshop will cover.
- Quick community check-in: “What brought you here / what do you hope to learn?”

0:10–0:30 – Composting basics (talk + visual)
- What composting is and why it matters (waste reduction, soil health).
- Greens vs browns, air, moisture, and time.
- Show simple visual/flipchart: ingredients, “do/don’t” list, basic ratio.

0:30–1:10 – Hands-on demo
- Walk to the active pile:
  - Show structure (layers, size, where air gets in).
  - Demonstrate turning the pile with a fork/shovel.
- Invite participants to:
  - Help turn the pile (with gloves).
  - Add a small amount of “greens” and “browns” to see layering.
- Show finished compost sample:
  - Look, feel, and smell; what “done” compost looks like.
- Talk through troubleshooting:
  - Too wet/too dry, smelly piles, critters, etc.

1:10–1:30 – Applying it at home
- Options: backyard bins, piles, community drop-off, worm bins (if relevant).
- How to set up something small at home with common materials.
- Answer practical questions (space constraints, winter composting basics, etc.).

1:30–1:50 – Q&A and informal discussion
- Open Q&A.
- Invite people to share their experiences and local tips.

1:50–2:00 – Wrap-up
- Summarize key points: recipe, greens/browns, air & moisture.
- Share where they can get more info (website/email, upcoming events).
- Encourage folks to check back on the garden’s compost pile later in the season.

If you’d like, next I can:
- Draft a short, ready-to-post workshop blurb (for email, social, or flyers), and/or
- Help you refine the signage text and a one-page handout for participants. What would be most useful next? </action>
